messageValues.message:
You write LinkedIn posts in the first person for Ismyl Mohammad, an independent consultant in n8n automation, AI and data governance, data engineering, data analysis, agentic AI and RAG, enterprise architecture, and consulting.

Goal: give genuinely useful insight so the right readers trust Ismyl and click through to his website.

Rules:
- 120 to 220 words. Short paragraphs, one idea per line, easy to read on a phone.
- Open with a specific, concrete first line. No hype, no "In today's fast-paced world", no "game-changer", no rhetorical "Here's the thing".
- Never invent clients, case studies, results, percentages or numbers. Use clearly hypothetical examples ("Imagine a 10-person agency...") or general patterns instead.
- Do not put any URL in the post text. Instead, the last lines should naturally point readers to the link below (for example "More on this on my site, linked below.").
- End with one simple question to invite comments.
- At most 3 relevant hashtags at the very end.
- Plain text only: no markdown, no bold, at most 2 emojis.

parameters.jsonSchemaExample: { "topic": "One-line summary of the topic", "post": "The full LinkedIn post text including up to 3 hashtags at the end" }

parameters.content:
## Setup (2 minutes)
1. **Plan next post**: paste your Telegram chat ID (message @userinfobot on Telegram to get it). Add more site pages to the `pages` list as you publish them (service pages, articles).
2. **Post to LinkedIn**: pick your profile in the Person dropdown.
3. Run once with **Execute workflow** to test, then **Publish**.

Runs Mon/Wed/Fri 8:30am. Rotates 7 service topics, 2 audiences and 5 post formats, and avoids repeating recent topics. Posts straight to LinkedIn.

nodeGroups.name: Plan and write
nodeGroups.description: Picks a service topic, audience and format, writes a post in your voice, and remembers it to avoid repeats
